J18.9 — Pneumonia, unspecified organism
Reason for admission
Community-acquired pneumonia with hypoxemia
Hospital course
The patient was admitted from the emergency department with community-acquired pneumonia (right
basilar crackles on examination) and hypoxemia (SpO2 90% on room air). She received IV ceftriaxone and
azithromycin and supplemental oxygen at 2 L/min. Fever resolved on hospital day 2, oxygen was
discontinued on 9/16, and white blood cell count decreased from 15.8 to 11.6. Blood cultures showed no
growth at 48 hours. She was discharged on oral amoxicillin-clavulanate to complete a 7-day course.

First recorded (9/14/2026 08:15 UTC): Temp 38.7 °C, HR 112 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 90%, BP 134/82 mmHg

Date
7/20/2026 15:00 UTC
Author
Dr. Thomas Byrne, MD — Endocrinology
Service
Endocrinology
Reason for consultation
Type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia following an emergency department visit on 6/22/2026.
Interval history
Started insulin glargine 10 units nightly in the ED and empagliflozin 10 mg daily on 7/1. Home fasting
glucose 150-190 mg/dL over the last week. No symptomatic hypoglycemia. Diet and activity reviewed.
Examination
Weight 101.6 kg. Blood pressure 136/84 mmHg. Feet: intact monofilament sensation, no ulcers.
Assessment
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; HbA1c 10.4% on 6/22/2026. Renal function preserved
(creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, eGFR 85).
Recommendations
1. Increase insulin glargine from 10 to 14 units nightly.
2. Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily and empagliflozin 10 mg daily.
3. Repeat HbA1c in approximately 3 months.
4. Referral for diabetic eye examination.
5. Return to endocrinology in 3 months.
Vital signs at visit
Heart rate 80 bpm; Systolic blood pressure 136 mmHg; Diastolic blood pressure 84 mmHg; Body weight
101.6 kg

Diagnoses
I50.23 — Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Reason for admission
Worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea and leg swelling
Hospital course
The patient was admitted with acute on chronic systolic heart failure and volume overload (admission
weight 84.2 kg, BNP 1480 pg/mL). She was diuresed with IV furosemide 40 mg twice daily with net negative
fluid balance; weight decreased to 80.1 kg at discharge and BNP decreased to 620 pg/mL. Potassium was
3.6 mmol/L on admission and 4.0 mmol/L on 9/2; creatinine was 1.1 to 1.2 mg/dL. Oral furosemide was
increased from 20 mg to 40 mg daily and spironolactone 12.5 mg daily was started. She received
heart-failure education including daily weights and sodium restriction.
Vital signs
First recorded (8/30/2026 16:30 UTC): Temp 36.8 °C, HR 98 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 91%, Weight 84.2 kg,
BP 148/88 mmHg

Reason for admission
Elective right total knee arthroplasty for primary osteoarthritis
Hospital course
The patient underwent an uncomplicated elective right total knee arthroplasty on 7/28/2026 under spinal
anesthesia. She received perioperative cefazolin and began enoxaparin 40 mg daily for venous
thromboembolism prophylaxis. Hemoglobin was 13.2 g/dL pre-operatively, 10.6 g/dL on post-operative day
1 and 10.9 g/dL on day 2; no transfusion was required. Pain decreased from 6/10 to 4/10 on acetaminophen
with oxycodone as needed. She ambulated with a walker and was discharged home with outpatient
physical therapy.

4. Return to nephrology in 3 months.
